name: Messenger
overview: The Bible presents messengers as divinely appointed agents who communicate God's word and prepare the way for His work. In the Old Testament, figures like the priests and prophets serve as messengers, entrusted with delivering God's law and guidance, as seen in Malachi where the priest is called the messenger of the LORD of hosts. God's promise to send a messenger to prepare the way before Him is highlighted in Malachi and affirmed in Matthew, pointing to the role of prophetic heralds like Elijah and John the Baptist. These messengers function both literally and figuratively to turn hearts toward God and announce His covenant, emphasizing their vital role in God's redemptive plan.
